newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT hikes prices as paper sales surge.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT hikes prices as paper sales surge.

text.p: Dutch paper, printing and office machinery group KNP BT said on Tuesday runaway demand had enabled its Austrian paper unit KNP Leykam to raise prices by some 5-10 percent in September.
But a company spokesman cautioned that rising prices for raw materials meant margins were still under pressure.
"Surging sales volumes are not necessarily an indication of better margins," spokesman Frans van Westen said. "It remains to be seen whether they will improve."
Van Westen said the usual slowdown in orders over the summer months had not happened.
"Volumes are good, there has been no summer lull," he said. Clients had been building up their inventories after the destocking of the first half, he said.
Paper machines were running at full capacity and orders for woodfree coated papers were subject to a waiting period of four weeks, he said.
KNP Leykam chairman Wolfgang Pfarl told journalists late last month that it was still too early to say whether the surge in sales volumes would enable the unit to break even in 1996.
In the first half, KNP Leykam, which is 72 percent owned by KNP BT, posted a loss of 24 million guilders on turnover of 1.1 billion guilders.
